mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about average power is correct?

options.A: Average power is the product of the constant force applied and the object's instantaneous velocity.
options.B: Average power equals the total work done divided by the total time taken.
options.C: Average power is the same as instantaneous power at any moment.
options.D: Average power does not depend on the time interval over which the work is done.

mcqs.answer: Average power equals the total work done divided by the total time taken.
mcqs.explanation: Average power is defined as the work done (or energy transferred) divided by the time interval over which the work is performed, P_avg = W/Δt. It is not the product of force and instantaneous velocity (that gives instantaneous power), nor is it independent of the time interval. Hence option B is correct.

mcqs.question: A constant force of 10 N acts on a particle moving along a straight line. At a particular instant the particle’s velocity is 4 m s⁻¹. Which reasoning correctly gives the instantaneous power at that instant?

options.A: Power = force × instantaneous velocity = 10 N × 4 m s⁻¹ = 40 W because power is the product of force and the velocity at that instant.
options.B: Power = force × average velocity over the whole motion, because power depends on average values.
options.C: Power = work done divided by total time, because instantaneous power is the same as average power.
options.D: Power = change in kinetic energy divided by the displacement, because power is energy per distance.

mcqs.answer: Power = force × instantaneous velocity = 10 N × 4 m s⁻¹ = 40 W because power is the product of force and the velocity at that instant.
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power is defined as the time derivative of work, P = dW/dt, which for a particle moving under a force becomes P = F·v (dot product). Using the instantaneous velocity (4 m s⁻¹) gives P = 10 N × 4 m s⁻¹ = 40 W. The other options misuse average quantities or confuse power with other concepts.

mcqs.question: Two machines each perform 500 J of work. Machine A completes the work in 5 s, while Machine B takes 20 s. Which statement correctly compares their powers?

options.A: Machine A’s power is four times that of Machine B.
options.B: Machine B’s power is four times that of Machine A.
options.C: Both machines have the same power because they do the same amount of work.
options.D: Power cannot be compared without knowing the forces involved.

mcqs.answer: Machine A’s power is four times that of Machine B.
mcqs.explanation: Power = work/time. For Machine A: P = 500 J / 5 s = 100 W. For Machine B: P = 500 J / 20 s = 25 W. Thus Machine A’s power is 100 W / 25 W = 4 times that of Machine B. The amount of work alone does not determine power; the time taken does.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A constant horizontal force accelerates a 1000 kg car from rest to 20 m s⁻¹ in 10 s. What is the average power supplied by the force during this interval?
mcqs.explanation: The work done equals the change in kinetic energy: ΔKE = ½ m v² = 0.5 × 1000 kg × (20 m s⁻¹)² = 200 000 J. Average power = work/time = 200 000 J / 10 s = 20 000 W = 20 kW. Although the instantaneous power at the final speed would be higher (P = F·v = 2000 N × 20 m s⁻¹ = 40 kW), the question asks for average power, giving 20 kW.

mcqs.question: Average power is defined as:
mcqs.explanation: Average power quantifies how quickly work is performed or energy is transferred, and is given by P_avg = W/Δt. Option B describes instantaneous power, while C and D refer to different physical quantities.

mcqs.question: Instantaneous power at a given moment is best expressed as:

options.A: Total work divided by total time.
options.C: Change in kinetic energy per hour.

mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power is the derivative of work with respect to time, P = dW/dt. For a particle under a force, this becomes the scalar product P = F·v, i.e., force times the instantaneous velocity component in the direction of the force. Options A and D describe average quantities, and C mixes units incorrectly.

mcqs.question: A constant force of 15 N moves an object through a displacement of 30 m in 5 s. Which expression correctly gives the power?
mcqs.explanation: Work done = force × displacement = 15 N × 30 m = 450 J. Power = work/time = 450 J / 5 s = 90 J/s, which is equivalent to 90 W. Option D explicitly shows the correct unit J/s (watts). Options A and C give the numeric value but omit the proper unit derivation, while B incorrectly labels the result as joules (energy).

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A conveyor belt moves at 2 m s⁻¹ and a constant horizontal force of 50 N pushes a box along the belt at constant speed. What is the power required to keep the box moving?
mcqs.explanation: When speed is constant, power needed to overcome the applied force is P = F·v. Here, F = 50 N and v = 2 m s⁻¹, so P = 50 N × 2 m s⁻¹ = 100 W. The other options correspond to incorrect multiplications.
